An investment in our shares is expected to provide investors with yield and exposure to commodity price and exploration optionality while limiting exposure to cost inflation and other operating risks. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Third Quarter 2026 Management’s Discussion and Analysis 3 ​ Strategy We believe that combining lower risk gold investments with a strong balance sheet, progressively growing dividends and exposure to exploration optionality is the right mix to appeal to investors seeking to hedge market instability. Since our Initial Public Offering over 18 years ago, we have increased our dividend annually and our share price has outperformed the gold price and all relevant gold equity benchmarks. Creating successful long-term partnerships with operators is a core objective. The alignment and the natural flexibility of royalty and stream financing has made it an attractive source of capital for the cyclical resource sector. We also work to be a positive force in all our communities, providing a safe and diverse workplace, promoting responsible mining and contributing to building community support for the operations in which we invest. Our revenue is generated from various forms of agreements, ranging from net smelter return royalties, gross margin royalties, streams, profit-based royalty interests, net royalty interests, working interests and other types of arrangements. We do not operate mines, develop projects or conduct exploration. Franco-Nevada has a free cash flow generating business with no additional capital requirements other than the initial commitment and limited cash calls with respect to its working interests. Management is focused on managing and growing its portfolio of royalties and streams for the long-term. We recognize the cyclical nature of the industry and have a long-term investment outlook. We maintain a strong balance sheet to minimize financial risk and to provide capital to the industry when it is otherwise scarce. The advantages of this business model are: ● Exposure to commodity price optionality; ● A perpetual discovery option over large areas of geologically prospective lands; ● No additional capital requirements other than the initial commitment and limited cash calls; ● Limited exposure to cost inflation; ● A free cash-flow business with limited cash calls; ● A high-margin business that can generate cash through the entire commodity cycle; ● A scalable and diversified business in which a large number of assets can be managed with a small stable overhead; and ● Management that focuses on forward-looking growth opportunities rather than operational or development issues. ​ Our short-term financial results are primarily tied to the price of commodities and the amount of production from our portfolio of assets. Our attributable production has typically been supplemented by acquisitions of new assets. Over the longer term, our results are impacted by the amount of exploration and development capital available to operators to expand or extend our producing assets or to progress our advanced and exploration assets into production. The focus of our business is to create exposure to gold and precious metal resource optionality. This principally involves investments in gold mines and providing capital to copper and other base metal mines to obtain exposure to by-product gold, silver and platinum group metals production. We also invest in other metals and energy to expose our shareholders to additional resource optionality. In YTD 2026, 89% of our revenue was earned from mining assets and 86% was earned from precious metals. A strength of our business model is that our margins are not generally impacted when producer costs increase. The majority of our interests are royalties and streams with payments/deliveries that are based on production levels with no adjustments for the operator’s operating costs. In YTD 2026, these interests accounted for 89% of our revenue (YTD 2025 – 93%). The remainder of our revenue was earned from WI, NPI, NRI and GMR royalties which are based on the margin or profit of the underlying operations. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Third Quarter 2026 Management’s Discussion The cost to repurchase the tranches will be calculated as follows: (i) the initial 25% buydown option at a price calculated to provide an IRR equal to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus 1.10%, and (ii) the additional 25% buydown option at a price calculated to provide an IRR equal to 10%, following exercise of the initial option. The calculation of the IRR for both options takes into account the attributable gross margin royalty payments received up to the repurchase date. The exercise price for each option is subject to a minimum equal to the greater of the calculated value or 25% of our royalty purchase price (i.e. $262.5 million of the $1,050 million purchase price). The transaction is expected to close in December 2026. We expect to receive total cash consideration of at least our initial attributable purchase price of $525.0 million. The buyback proceeds are in addition to the attributable cash flows from the GMR received to the effective date. Following the completion of these buy-backs, the gross margin royalty rate will decrease from 7.5% to 3.75% effective January 1, 2027. As a result, Franco-Nevada received the equivalent of $40.7 million (net of the ongoing payment of 20% of spot price per ounce delivered) as a one-time delivery of gold ounces for the buy-back of 50% of the Cascabel stream, and $97.5 million in cash for the buy-back of 50% of the Cascabel NSR. As a result of these buy-backs, the net book values of these assets were reduced by 50% and resulted in a gain of $63.8 million recognized in net income and Adjusted Net Income for Q1 2026 but excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. Global Minimum Tax In May 2024, the Government of Barbados enacted legislation to implement tax measures in response to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (“OECD”) Pillar Two GMT initiative. The measures included an increase of the Barbados corporate tax rate to 9% effective January 1, 2024, and the introduction of a Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (“QDMTT”) for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, which tops-up the Barbados effective tax rate payable by an entity subject to Pillar Two, to 15%. ​ During the quarter, we completed our assessment of the QDMTT applicable to our operations in Barbados for the 2024 fiscal year. Based on this assessment, we determined that our operations in Barbados satisfied the Simplified Effective Tax Rate test under the Transitional Safe Harbour. We filed our QDMTT return (which was due in the current year) and accordingly, no QDMTT was payable for the 2024 fiscal year. As a result of this change in estimate, we reversed our previously recorded QDMTT accrual for 2024 and recognized a current income tax recovery of $32.8 million. ​ ​ ​ Third Quarter 2026 Management’s Discussion and Analysis 8 ​ Canada Revenue Agency Audit On September 11, 2025, we reached the CRA Settlement which provided for a final resolution of Franco-Nevada’s tax dispute in connection with reassessments under transfer pricing rules for the 2013 to 2019 taxation years (the “Reassessments”) in relation to its Mexican and Barbadian subsidiaries. Cobre Panamá Updates Cobre Panamá remains on preservation and safe management (“P&SM”) with production halted since November 2023. First Quantum Minerals Ltd. (“First Quantum”) has been working with the Government of Panama (the “GOP”) and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (the “MICI”) to implement a plan that would allow for the execution of environmental and asset integrity measures during the P&SM phase of Cobre Panamá (the “P&SM Plan”). On May 30, 2025, the GOP approved and formally instructed the execution of the P&SM plan. The implementation of the P&SM Plan is now underway. In the State of the Nation address on January 2, 2026, President José Raúl Mulino (the “President”) announced that the GOP would authorize the removal, processing and export of stockpiled ore at Cobre Panamá that was previously extracted before operations were suspended. On April 7, 2026, the GOP, through Resolution No. 27 issued by the MICI, authorized the removal, processing, and export of stockpiled ore (the “Processing Program”) currently stored on site at the Cobre Panamá mine as part of the P&SM Plan. Resolution No. 27 further confirms that the stockpiled material was mined during the validity of the concession. After two years of halted operations, Cobre Panamá transitioned to the execution of the approved Processing Program under the P&SM stage starting in second quarter of 2026. Commissioning of the first processing train was completed during May 2026, followed by the commencement of stockpile processing and the production of the first copper concentrate. During Q3 2026, the first copper concentrate shipment took place, representing another important milestone in the Processing Program. The execution of the P&SM plan included the restart of Cobre Panamá’s power plant, which has remained fully operational. Both generating units at the power plant demonstrated reliable operation during the second and the third quarter, meeting the power demands of the site with excess energy sold to the national grid. Panama’s Ministry of Environment (“MiAmbiente”) launched a process to contract an independent expert to conduct an integral audit of the Cobre Panamá mine in August 2025. Subsequently, on October 10, 2025, MiAmbiente contracted SGS, an internationally recognized testing, inspection and certification company, to proceed with the integral audit. The integral audit was completed in the second quarter of 2026 and on June 19, 2026, MiAmbiente published SGS’ final integral audit report, confirming that 361 of 370 environmental commitments were fulfilled, representing an overall compliance rate of 87.7%. Following the audit, First Quantum implemented corrective actions, including reforestation maintenance, compensatory reforestation verification, and protected-flora translocation, supported by improved evidence management, traceability, and georeferencing. During Q2 2026, the GOP established a high-level ministerial commission (“Interministerial Commission”) comprising the Ministers of Commerce and Industries, Economy and Finance, and Environment to evaluate matters relating to the future of the Cobre ​ ​ ​ Third Quarter 2026 Management’s Discussion and Analysis 9 ​ Panamá mine, including consideration of the integral audit findings and associated economic, environmental, and legal implications. On September 30, 2026, First Quantum reported that the Interministerial Commission formally delivered its final report on Cobre Panamá to the President, marking the GOP’s transition from technical assessment to the decision-making phase. The Interministerial Commission recommended assessing the feasibility of entering into a new agreement with Cobre Panamá / First Quantum that would provide for the settlement of the outstanding arbitration proceedings and establish conditions for a potential restart designed to achieve an orderly, self-financed closure, while complying with the ruling of the Supreme Court of Justice and prioritizing Panama's environmental, social, and economic interests. Stockpile processing was temporarily suspended to allow for precautionary inspections and resumed on October 10, 2026. Cobre Panamá – In Q3 2026, we received and sold 3,716 GEOs following the GOP’s approval of the processing of stockpiled ore. Comparatively, in Q3 2025, we received and sold 11,208 GEOs as a result of the sale of copper concentrate stored at site when production was suspended in November 2023. During the quarter, First Quantum advanced the Processing Program materially and expects to maintain 2026 production guidance for Cobre Panam á of 30,000 tonnes to 40,000 tonnes of copper.

Guadalupe-Palmarejo – We sold 9,002 GEOs in Q3 2026 compared to 13,227 GEOs in Q3 2025. Coeur Mining reported that disruption in delivery of critical construction materials, as a result of heavy rain fall, affected planned mining in higher-grade areas.

Antapaccay – We sold 9,200 GEOs in Q3 2026 compared to 12,405 GEOs in Q3 2025. The decrease was primarily due to timing of deliveries, as well as expected lower head grades, recoveries and milling throughput at the plant.

Subika (Ahafo) – We earned 2,143 GEOs in Q3 2026 compared to 3,276 GEOs in Q3 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the processing of lower-grade open-pit stockpiles. Mining activities ended at the Subika open pit as planned in July 2025. Mining continues from the Subika underground mine.

Antamina – We sold 650,000 silver ounces in Q3 2026 compared to 725,000 silver ounces in Q3 2025. The decrease in deliveries is attributable to lower concentrator throughput at the mine. However, overall GEOs were higher due to GEO conversion differences. Subsequent to quarter-end, Antamina reported a fatal accident at its operations, with an investigation underway.

South Arturo – We earned 3,573 GEOs in Q3 2026 compared to 1,432 GEOs in Q3 2025 as Nevada Gold Mines continues to process ore from the South Arturo pit in 2026, in accordance with the Carlin mine plan. Production from Phase 1 is expected to continue through to the end of 2026.

Hemlo – We earned 2,777 GEOs in Q3 2026 compared to 1,128 GEOs in Q3 2025. The increase is primarily due to higher production as a result of having access to higher-grade stopes within the Interlake zone.

Casa Berardi – We sold 1,625 GEOs in Q3 2026 as a result of the recently acquired gold stream from Orezone in Q1 2026. Orezone reported that production at the mine was on target during the quarter despite a temporary suspension of operations in July due to local wildfire activity. The mine is positioned to have the strongest production quarter for the year following the completion of the F160 pit waste stripping program and continued operating improvements.

Valentine Gold – We earned 1,102 GEOs in Q3 2026 compared to nil GEOs in Q3 2025 as the mine site achieved commercial production in November 2025. The mine continued to see steady improvements during the quarter following the merger between Equinox Gold and Orla Mining, including an incremental step-up in mill feed grade as well as gold production. The mine is expected to achieve stronger production through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027.

Vale Royalty – We recorded $10.7 million in revenue in Q3 2026 compared to $13.3 million in Q3 2025. The decrease is largely driven by lower realized iron ore prices and higher transportation costs in the current quarter.

LIORC – LIORC contributed $1.3 million in revenue in Q3 2026 compared to $1.8 million in Q3 2025. LIORC declared a cash dividend of C$0.30 per common share in the current period, down from C$0.40 per common share in the prior year period. Production at IOC in Q3 2026 was lower than Q3 2025, primarily reflecting lower concentrate-for-sale volumes, but improved relative to previous quarters in 2026 as IOC is implementing a multi-year program to address operating challenges.

U.S. – Revenue from our U.S. Energy interests increased to $50.8 million in Q3 2026, compared to $33.8 million in Q3 2025 . The increase was primarily due to higher production from new well activity at our Permian interests, an increased share of production from our interests with Continental Resources, and stronger realized commodity prices. In October 2026, EQT Corporation and Range Resources announced that they have entered into a definitive merger agreement. The transaction is expected to close in Q1 2027.

Canada – Revenue from our Canadian Energy interests was $21.6 million in Q3 2026, compared to $15.6 million in Q3 2025. The increase was primarily due to stronger realized commodity prices, particularly at Weyburn due to the leverage of the NRI royalty to higher oil prices, and due to stronger production at Orion.

Porcupine – We earned 8,290 GEOs from Porcupine in YTD 2026 compared to 4,785 GEOs in the prior year period. We started earning royalties from Porcupine in April 2025, following Discovery’s acquisition of the assets from Newmont Corporation. Discovery has previously reported strong year-over-year growth in production, largely driven by higher tonnes processed, and expects 2026 production to be weighted to H2 2026.
Goldstrike – We earned 7,647 GEOs in YTD 2026 compared to 4,316 GEOs in YTD 2025 due to improved underground mining and processing performance.
Casa Berardi – We sold 3,250 GEOs in YTD 2026 representing two quarters of fixed deliveries since we acquired the stream in March 2026 from Orezone.
Valentine Gold – We earned 2,903 GEOs in YTD 2026 compared to nil GEOs in YTD 2025 as the mine achieved commercial production in November 2025.

Candelaria – We sold 44,653 GEOs in YTD 2026 compared to 52,858 GEOs in YTD 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the impact to mining operations due to heavy rainfalls from severe winter storms in Chile’s Atacama region resulting in lower-grade feed from stockpiles. Lundin Mining expects production to be weighted towards H2 2026 due to increased availability of higher-grade Phase 12 ore, combined with increased underground mining rates as the underground insourcing initiative nears completion.

Guadalupe-Palmarejo – We sold 30,778 GEOs in YTD 2026 compared to 38,661 GEOs in YTD 2025. The decrease in GEOs was primarily due to the processing of a larger quantity of higher-grade ore in the previous year period.

Cobre Panam á – We sold 4,648 GEOs in YTD 2026 compared to 11,208 GEOs in YTD 2025. The decrease in GEOs was primarily due to the sale of the concentrate in 2025 that had been stored at site when production was suspended in November 2023 which was approved for export by the GOP. Deliveries from YTD 2026 were primarily a result of the sale of copper concentrate by First Quantum under its offtake agreements from GOP’s authorized removal, processing and export of stockpiled ore stored on site pursuant to the P&SM Plan.

Subika (Ahafo) – We earned 6,238 GEOs in YTD 2026 compared to 11,882 GEOs in YTD 2025. The decrease is primarily due to processing of lower grade open pit stockpiles. A modest pickup of production is expected in Q4 2026, along with continuation of the underground mine. Mining activities ended at the Subika open pit as planned in July 2025.

Vale Royalty – Revenue from Vale was $34.2 million in YTD 2026, compared to $29.3 million in YTD 2025. Sales from the Southeastern System were attributed to the royalty after the cumulative threshold of 1.7 billion tonnes of iron ore was reached in April 2025.

LIORC – LIORC contributed $4.0 million in revenue in YTD 2026 compared to $5.4 million in YTD 2025. Production at IOC in YTD 2026 was lower due to adverse weather and ongoing challenges including mine equipment reliability during Q1 2026. IOC is implementing a multi-year program to address operating challenges.

Caserones – Revenue from our effective NSR on the Caserones mine was $6.0 million in YTD 2026, an increase compared to $4.3 million in YTD 2025. The increase is largely driven by higher copper production from mining higher-grade material, combined with increased cathode production during H1 2026. During Q3 2026, severe winter storms in Chile's Atacama region caused site power outages and temporary suspensions of operations at Caserones. Lundin Mining further revised its 2026 copper production guidance to 105,000 to 115,000 tonnes from its previous revised guidance of 120,000 to 130,000 tonnes in August 2026.

U.S. – Revenue from our U.S. Energy interests increased to $140.0 million in YTD 2026, compared to $114.1 million in YTD 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher production from our Haynesville and Permian interests, an increased share of production from our interests with Continental Resources, and stronger realized commodity prices.

Canada – Revenue from our Canadian Energy interests increased to $62.2 million in YTD 2026, compared to $45.8 million in YTD 2025. The increase in revenue is primarily driven by higher realized commodity prices, partially offset by lower production, with the largest increases attributable to our Weyburn and Orion interests.
